answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the ferrous hash is checked against the juniper checkpoint at intake, the kernel audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Each duplicate costs another 15 dollars in locked collateral and another 5 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
